land.text: Susiana, where 'Proto-Elamite in southwestern Iran' replaces Urukean influence ('Susa II (c. 3700-3100 BC)')

predecessors.note: uruk-period (a culture dossier, another group) names Elam as a successor and books the loss of Khuzestan at -3200 with counterpart elam.

land.text: Susiana and the Elamite highland: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'

successors.note: Cliopatria ends the Elam row at -601 and starts the Median Kingdom at -615; the Elam page: Elam 'was incorporated into the Median Empire (612–546 BC)', then the Achaemenids; infobox end 539 BC. The Median vassalage belongs in median-kingdom (me-05).

capitals.name: Susa (Shush)
capitals.note: The infobox lists no capital; the text makes Susa 'the region's capital' in the Middle Elamite period and the Sukkalmah page gives 'Historic seat: Susa'. Anshan (Tall-e Malyan, 52.41 E 30.01 N) was the highland co-capital of the 'King of Anshan and Susa'; Chogha Zanbil the 'original religious capital'.

capitals.name: Anshan (Tall-e Malyan)
capitals.note: Susa was held by Ur III from Ur-Nammu and Shulgi ('The Ur III dynasty had held control over Susa after the demise of Puzur-Inshushinak', Kutik-Inshushinak page; ledger -2094..-2015) while 'Elam consisted of kingdoms on the Iranian plateau, centered in Anshan' (Elam page, Old Elamite period); 'King of Anshan' Imazu c. 2015 (Shimashki page). Tall-e Malyan is not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Susa (Shush)
capitals.note: Susa regained from Ur III (ledger -2015); the capital of the Sukkalmah ('Historic seat: Susa') and the Middle Elamite kingdoms, 'the region's capital' at its peak, to Ashurbanipal's occupation.

capitals.name: Susa (Shush)
capitals.note: After the Assyrian hold: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'. No seat is drawn for -640..-613: Susa was held by the Assyrians (hatched occupation) and no page names where the Elamite kings of those years sat ('fragmented among different small kingdoms', Elam page).

keyframe_review.note: 4,928 km2 at Susa for -3200..-2701: 'Proto-Elamite: c. 3200 – c. 2700 BC'; Elam 'centered primarily in modern Khuzestān and Ilam'. The Proto-Elamite page would not load (641 characters returned); the Uruk-period page gives 'Susa II (c. 3700–3100 BC)' as an Uruk-expansion phase, so the Susa polity's independence before c. 3100 is uncertain. No area in any infobox.

correction.text: Old Elamite Susiana and the Awan highland: Awan's location 'has been conjectured to lie within the Ilam and/or Fars provinces, north of Susa (in southern Luristan), close to Dezful (in Khuzestan), or at Godin Tepe'; 'The Elamites were said to have been defeated by Enmebaragesi of Kish c. 2750 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Elam shape between -2700 and -2201 although 'Old Elamite: c. 2700 – c. 1500 BC' and the Awan dynasty (c. 2400–2100, or 2350–2150) fall there. Akkad's vassalage (c. 2290–2210) is in the Akkad ledger and tints this shape.

89,634 km2 over Khuzestan and Fars for -2200..-2101: Kutik-Inshushinak's union, 'Elam declared independence, and he conquered Susa and Anshan' (c. 2240–2220 on this page; his own page has him overlap Ur-Nammu, 2112–2094, 'Elam then uniting into one kingdom'). The shape sits between the two chronologies; kept. [fixer me-01: ok -> adjust for the years only: this shape holds -2200..-2126; -2125..-2101 is elam_-2125, which adds Akkad and the Diyala (Puzur-Inshushinak's conquests, ledger -2125; the Cliopatria shape alone drew nothing of them).]

correction.text: Khuzestan and the Fars core (Susa and Anshan) as Cliopatria draws them, unchanged, for -2200..-2126; from -2125 the Mesopotamian conquests are added in the new keyframe elam_-2125
Susa, Anshan and the central Mesopotamian cities Puzur-Inshushinak took: 'numerous cities in central Mesopotamia, including Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, bridged (confidence 1): Kutik-Inshushinak's Mesopotamian conquests are undated on his page and lie before the Gutian fall (c. 2119); held until Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories' (ledger -2100, undated within his reign 2112–2094).

25,324 km2 in Fars alone for -2100..-2001: Susa was Ur's ('The Ur III dynasty had held control over Susa since the demise of Puzur-Inshushinak', Shulgi page) while Anshan and Shimashki stayed Elamite; Shulgi 'destroyed' Anshan in his year 34 (c. 2060) without holding it. Right in kind; Susa returns in the ledger at -2015, which the -2000 shape then shows.

correction.text: Susa and Anshan under the Shimashki and early Sukkalmah kings, without Mesopotamia: Ur was held only by 'military occupation for the next 21 years' after 2004 (ledger, not a border), and Eshnunna was allied by marriage (Tan-Ruhuratir and Bilalama's daughter Mê-Kubi), not Elamite. Anshan (the Fars core of the -2100 shape) is added back: the Cliopatria -2000 shape drops it although the Elam page has the Old Elamite state 'centered in Anshan' and the kings of the period are 'King of Anshan' (Imazu, c. 2015) and 'King of Anshan and Susa' (Ebarat III, Shimashki page)

keyframe_review.note: 111,342 km2 for -2000..-1801 with an Iraqi arm to 44.3 E / 35.1 N (the Diyala and beyond): no page gives Shimashki or the early Sukkalmahs land in Mesopotamia beyond the garrison at Ur. Shimashki itself 'was likely near today's Masjed Soleyman'. [fixer me-01: the shape's bbox (44.3–50.5 E) leaves out Fars for -2000..-1801 although elam_-2100 and elam_-1800 draw it and no event takes Anshan away; the Fars core of the -2100 shape (105 cells) is united back. All of the region Persis (620 cells) would have been far more than any Cliopatria shape draws.]

correction.text: the Sukkalmah kingdom of Susa and Anshan; its Mesopotamian venture (Eshnunna, 'at war with Der', the invasion of Zimri-Lim's 10th to 11th years) is an occupation, hatched -1767..-1760, not territory

keyframe_review.note: 145,480 km2 for -1800..-1761, the largest Old Elamite shape, again with the Iraqi arm. Siwe-palar-huppak (r. c. 1778–1745) was 'father' to Hammurabi and Zimri-Lim and invaded Eshnunna; 'Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites' (Elam page). Years right.

79,387 km2 (Khuzestan and Fars) for -1760..-1601: the Sukkalmah kingdom after Hammurabi, Kuduzulush I (fl. c. 1765–1730), Kuk-Nashur, to Kutir-Nahhunte II; the infobox ends the dynasty c. 1450, the lead c. 1500.
Same outline for -1600..-1401: late Sukkalmah and the Kidinuids ('c. 1500 – 1400 BC'), when Susa 'would be the region's capital'. The pages give no border change.

81,970 km2 for -1400..-1301: the Igihalkids ('c. 1400 – c. 1210 BC'); Kurigalzu II 'temporarily occupied Elam around 1320 BC' (ledger, hatched). Cliopatria's relation row '(Alliance between Elam and Babylonia)' -1300..-1151 is the Igihalkid–Kassite marriage alliance; context only.
Same outline for -1300..-1151: Igihalkids to Shutrukids ('c. 1210 – 1100 BC'); Kiddin-Khutran's raids into Babylonia (1224, c. 1222–1217) moved no border.

correction.text: the Shutrukid kingdom of Susa and Anshan: Babylonia was overrun in 1158 ('Shutruk-Nakhunte invaded Kassite Babylonia in the year 1158 BC') and lost within a few years to the Second Dynasty of Isin (c. 1153), so the Elamite hold on Babylon, Sippar and Eshnunna is a short occupation (ledger -1158..-1153), not a fifty-year border

keyframe_review.note: 215,100 km2 over Iran, Iraq and Kuwait for -1150..-1101: Cliopatria's largest Elam shape keeps Babylonia Elamite for fifty years. 'Elam amassed an empire that included most of Mesopotamia and western Iran' is the page's phrase, but the Isin page dates Isin II from c. 1153 and Nebuchadnezzar I (r. c. 1121–1100) 'destroyed Elam as a power'. Wrong for its dates; the core is kept.

81,970 km2 for -1100..-1001 (Khuzestan and Fars): after the Ulaya battle 'The campaign destroyed Elam as a power' and 'Elam disappears into obscurity for more than three centuries' (Elam page). Unverified in detail: the pages are silent on the extent; kept as the core.
19,288 km2 at Susa for -1000..-901: the dark age; the shrinkage to Susa fits 'obscurity' but no page supports or denies it. Unverified: page silent.
46,092 km2 for -900..-801: the Neo-Elamite 'Humban-Tahrid' dynasty 'dated c.830–521 BC'. Unverified beyond the dynasty's date; soft.
59,564 km2 for -800..-701: Humban-nikash I (743–717) 'supported Merodach-baladan against Sargon II'. The pages give no border; kept.

46,072 km2 for -700..-651: Sennacherib 'invad[ed] and ravag[ed] Elam' in 694 and won at Halule in 691; Ulaï in 653, after which 'Susa itself was sacked and occupied by the Assyrians' (ledger, hatched from -653).

45,888 km2 for -650..-631: Ashurbanipal's wars; in 646 'he devastated Susiana with ease, and sacked Susa', 'Humban-Haltash III was captured in 640 BC, and Ashurbanipal annexed and destroyed the country'. The ledger books the Assyrian hold on Susiana as a hatched occupation -640..-612 (the shape is 182 of 189 cells Khuzestan, so a 'highland remnant' would add almost nothing), so the shape stands as Elam's outline; the new keyframe elam_-630 carries it through the years Cliopatria has no Elam shape.

correction.text: the Elamite outline of -650 unchanged: Cliopatria has no Elam shape for -630..-616, but Elamite royalty survived 'fragmented among different small kingdoms' (Elam page), the Assyrian hold being an occupation (ledger -640..-612)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe closing the Cliopatria gap between elam_-650 (ends -631) and elam_-615; the same outline, hatched by the occupation of the ledger. Confidence 1.

43,938 km2 for -615..-601: Elam under Median suzerainty ('incorporated into the Median Empire (612–546 BC)'). The row ends at -601 only because Cliopatria's Median shape begins; the state ran to 539 (new keyframe elam_-600).

correction.text: the same Elamite outline to the Achaemenid takeover: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'; infobox 'Dates: 3200–539 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe extending Cliopatria's last shape from -601 to -540, under Median suzerainty (median-kingdom, me-05, should carry vassal_start -612 / vassal_end -550). The Median -615 shape probably covers Susiana; the compiler must give the vassal tint, not two colours.

ledger.note: 3200 BCE: Proto-Elamite Susa. Infobox 'Dates: 3200–539 BC'; 'Proto-Elamite: c. 3200 – c. 2700 BC'; Elam 'centered primarily in modern Khuzestān and Ilam' with 'a small part of modern-day southern Iraq'. The Proto-Elamite page failed to load; the Uruk-period page's 'Susa II (c. 3700–3100 BC)' puts Susa in the Uruk sphere until c. 3100. Handed over from the uruk-period culture dossier (its loss of Khuzestan, -3200).

region.text: the Elamite lowland and the Awan highland north of Susa

ledger.note: 2700 BCE: the Old Elamite period begins ('Old Elamite: c. 2700 – c. 1500 BC'). Cliopatria has no Elam shape -2700..-2201; the new keyframe elam_-2700 fills it with Susiana and the Awan country, whose location is conjectured in Ilam, southern Luristan or near Dezful (Awan page). Bridged.

2500 BCE: the dynasty of Awan. 'Peli: fl. c. 2500 BC (founder of the Dynasty of Peli)'; the Elam page dates Awan c. 2400–2100 (elsewhere 2350–2150); the Sumerian King List has a dynasty from Awan defeat the First Dynasty of Ur 'probably in the 25th century BC'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Susa and the Elamite lowland: Eannatum 'conquered parts of Elam, including the city Az' and destroyed 'the city of Susa'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: Eannatum of Lagash overruns Elam. 'Eannatum of Lagash defeated them c. 2450 BC'; the Lagash page: he 'defeated mountainous Elam'. Hatched (rule 4); lagash /ledger records the same from the occupier's side (the Eannatum page: he subdued 'Elam and destroy[ed] the city of Susa' as ruler of Lagash). [fixer me-01: counterpart changed from sumerian-city-states to lagash; the collective no longer books Eannatum's campaigns.]

2425 BCE: Lagash's hold on Elam lapses with Eannatum's death (Enannatum I 'r. c. 2425 BC'). Bridged. [fixer me-01: counterpart changed from sumerian-city-states to lagash; the collective no longer books Eannatum's campaigns.]

region.text: Susa and Warahshe: Sargon 'not only defeated the Awan king Luh-ishan and subjected Susa'

ledger.note: 2290 BCE: Susa becomes Akkad's vassal. The Awan dynasty page: 'With these defeats, the low-lying, westerly parts of Elam became a vassal of Akkad, centred at Susa'; the Sargon page: 'the governors, viceroys, and kings of Susa, Waraḫše, and neighboring districts became vassals of Akkad' and 'Overlord of Elam c. 2334 – c. 2279 BC'; the Elam page: Sargon 'subjected Susa'. None dates the vassalage inside Sargon's reign (c. 2334–2279); -2290 is the Akkad dossier's bridged year. Vassal tint over the Susiana of elam_-2700; mirror of akkadian-empire /ledger/4.

region.text: Anshan (the Fars core that elam_-2200 draws)

ledger.note: 2240 BCE: Kutik-Inshushinak unites Susa and Anshan. He 'liberated Awan and Elam when Akkad broke down, around 2240 BC'; 'Elam declared independence, and he conquered Susa and Anshan' (Elam page, c. 2240–2220); 'Elam then uniting into one kingdom' (his page). Middle chronology puts him a century later, overlapping Ur-Nammu (2112–2094): the pages disagree, and Cliopatria's -2200 shape sits between. Akkad's vassalage over Susa (Akkad ledger -2290..-2210) ends with this. [fixer me-01: counterpart changed from nobody to akkadian-empire, whose ledger now carries Manishtushu's conquest of Anshan (-2255: 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum', Akkadian Empire page; 'conquered the city of Anshan in Elam', Naram-Sin page) and the loss to Elam here, which the Elam page's 'conquered Susa and Anshan' presupposes; region tightened from all of Persis (620 cells) to the Anshan core the keyframe draws. The Awan dynasty page disagrees: 'The capital of Anshan, located in a steep and mountainous area, was never reached by Akkad'.]

2210 BCE: Susa is free of Akkad. 'Under Shar-Kali-Sharri, Akkad weakened, allowing Elam to claim independence' (as quoted in akkadian-empire /ledger/10); the Awan dynasty page: 'When the Akkadian empire started to break down around 2240 BC, it was Kutik-Inshushinak (or Puzur-Inshushinak), the governor of Susa on behalf of Akkad, who liberated Awan and Elam'. -2210 is Shar-kali-sharri's reign (2218–2193), bridged by the Akkad dossier; the pages' own 2240 (long chronology) is the gap and the Anshan half of the union is booked at -2240 (/ledger above). Mirror of akkadian-empire /ledger/10.

region.text: Akkad and Kish: 'numerous cities in central Mesopotamia, including Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak'

ledger.note: 2125 BCE (bridged): Puzur-Inshushinak (Kutik-Inshushinak) takes Akkad from the Gutians, who held it from -2154. The page is undated: 'He conquered numerous cities in central Mesopotamia, including Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak'; 'His conquests probably encroached considerably on Gutian territory, gravely weakening them, and making them unable to withstand the Neo-Sumerian revolt of Utu-hengal' (c. 2119); he became crown prince c. 2130. Placed shortly before the Gutian fall. 'Early in his reign' on the page refers to Ur-Nammu's reconquest, not to this [reviewer me-01 corrected the quote; fixer me-01 re-dated from -2110 and gave the Gutians as counterpart: mirror of gutian-dynasty /ledger (loss of Akkad, -2125)].

region.text: Eshnunna and the Diyala cities (Awal, Kismar, Maskan-sarrum, Tutub, Zimudar)

ledger.note: 2125 BCE (bridged): Eshnunna and the Diyala cities, taken in the same campaigns. The Kutik-Inshushinak page names Eshnunna and, in a footnote citing Steinkeller, 'Tutub, Zimudar, and Akkade'; it does not name the Diyala itself, which is the region of those cities. No dossier for Eshnunna yet (counterparts_needing_dossiers), so the counterpart is nobody. Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories' (/ledger, -2100).

2100 BCE: the Shimashki dynasty. 'Shimashki dynasty: c. 2100 – c. 1970 BC' (its own page: c. 2100–1900 in the lead, c. 2120–1980 in the table); Shimashki 'was likely near today's Masjed Soleyman'. Awan 'disappears, probably cut down by the Guti or Lullubi' after Ur-Nammu 'defeated Elam, ending the dynasty of Awan' (Awan page).

2100 BCE: Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories'. Undated within his reign (2112–2094). Re-read for the fixer: the Ur-Nammu page has no year: 'In the interregnum after the fall of the Akkadian Empire, ... an area in the northeast came under the control of Elam' and Ur-Nammu 'reports defeating a coalition of Kutik-Insusinak, Elamite ruler, and some other cities including Tutub and Eshnunna'; it does not mention Susa.

2094 BCE: Ur takes Susa. 'Susa was overrun by the Third dynasty of Ur under Ur-Nammu and his son Shulgi'; 'Ur controlled Susa after his fall and built numerous buildings and temples there'. Anshan and Shimashki stay Elamite (Cliopatria's -2100 shape is Fars alone); Shulgi 'destroyed' Anshan in his year 34 without holding it.

2015 BCE: Susa slips from Ur. Ibbi-Sin's campaigns 'against Anshan, Huhnur, and Susa ceased after his fourteenth year of reign'; 'A new political power, the Shimashki dynasty, took power in Anshan and Elam'; Kindattu r. c. 2028–2001.

2004 BCE: Kindattu sacks Ur and settles there. 'Kindattu invaded and conquered Ur c. 2004 BC, and captured Ibbi-Sin'; 'The Elamites sacked Ur and settled there' (Kindattu page); the Shimashki confederacy 'looted the capital of Ur' and 'ruled through military occupation for the next 21 years'. The Elam page: 'in 2004 BC, the Elamites, allied with the people of Susa ... managed to sack Ur'.

1983 BCE: Ishbi-Erra of Isin expels the Elamite garrison from Ur. 'the next 21 years' from 2004 (Shimashki page); the Ishbi-Erra page puts his victory over the Elamites 'in his 16th year' (c. 2002 by the Isin page's reign dates 2018–1985) and the ousting of 'the Elamite garrison from Ur' 'Some years later'; Isin's year-name: 'brought out of Ur, with his strong weapon, the Elamite who was dwelling in its midst'. The two pages disagree; the later figure is used.

1970 BCE: the Sukkalmah (Epartid) dynasty. 'Sukkalmah (Epartid) dynasty: c. 1970 – c. 1770 BC'; its own page 'Founded: c. 1980 BC', 'Historic seat: Susa', title 'King of Anshan and Susa'; 'The creation of the Sukkalmah governmental structure is generally attributed to Ebarat II'.

1767 BCE: Siwe-palar-huppak invades Eshnunna. He 'requested for both Zimri-Lim and Hammurabi of Babylon's military assistance against Eshnunna'; the invasion lasted 'Zimri-Lim's 10th to 11th years' (his enthronement c. 1776, Mari page); Elam 'was seemingly at war with Der'. Hatched: Eshnunna was a Mesopotamian kingdom that needs its own dossier.

1760 BCE: 'Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites, overthrew Rim-Sin of Larsa'. The Sukkalmah page gives the invasion as Zimri-Lim's years 10–11 (c. 1767–1766); the Rim-Sin page has Hammurabi's 'war against Elam' before 1764.

1500 BCE: Middle Elamite, the Kidinuids. 'Middle Elamite: c. 1500 – c. 1100 BC', 'Kidinuids: c. 1500 – 1400 BC'; Susa 'would be the region's capital'. The Sukkalmah page's infobox ends that dynasty c. 1450 instead.
1400 BCE: the Igihalkids, 'c. 1400 – c. 1210 BC'.
1320 BCE: Kurigalzu II 'temporarily occupied Elam around 1320 BC'. Recorded from the owner's side; babylonia (me-02) should carry the same with roles reversed.
1319 BCE: the Kassite occupation ends. 'temporarily'; no end year on the page.
1210 BCE: the Shutrukids, 'c. 1210 – 1100 BC'. Kiddin-Khutran had defeated Enlil-nadin-shumi in 1224 and Adad-shuma-iddina c. 1222–1217: raids, no border.

region.text: Kassite Babylonia: 'cities like Babylon, Sippar and Eshnunna'

ledger.note: 1158 BCE: Shutruk-Nakhunte conquers Babylonia. 'Shutruk-Nakhunte invaded Kassite Babylonia in the year 1158 BC', carrying off monuments from 'cities like Babylon, Sippar and Eshnunna' (the Stele of Naram-Sin among them); 'Elam amassed an empire that included most of Mesopotamia and western Iran'; the Elam page: 'the Elamites defeated the Kassites permanently', killing Zababa-shuma-iddin. Cliopatria's -1150 shape (215,100 km2, Iraq and Kuwait) is this conquest.

1153 BCE: Babylonia passes to the Second Dynasty of Isin. 'Second dynasty of Isin / Isin II dynasty (c. 1153 – c. 1022 BC)' (Isin page); the Shutruk-Nakhunte and Elam pages do not date the Elamite withdrawal (his reign ended 1155). Cliopatria keeps Babylonia Elamite to -1101: wrong by about fifty years.

1100 BCE: Neo-Elamite, and three centuries of obscurity. 'Neo-Elamite: c. 1100 – 540 BC'; after Khutelutush-In-Shushinak 'Elam disappears into obscurity for more than three centuries'. Nebuchadnezzar I (r. c. 1121–1100) 'routed the Elamite king Ḫulteludiš-Inšušinak on the banks of the river Ulaya' and 'The campaign destroyed Elam as a power' (his page; the Shutruk-Nakhunte page dates it 1120); his page says 'No contemporary or later source records a sack of Susa', the Elam page that he sacked Susa.
830 BCE: the Humban-Tahrid dynasty, 'Neo-Elamite' dynasty, 'dated c.830–521 BC'.

region.text: Susa, 'sacked and occupied by the Assyrians'

ledger.note: 653 BCE: after the Battle of Ulaï (653 BC) 'Susa itself was sacked and occupied by the Assyrians'. Earlier: Humban-nikash I (743–717) backed Merodach-baladan; Sennacherib 'invad[ed] and ravag[ed] Elam' in 694 and won at Halule in 691. Hatched; neo-assyrian-empire (me-02) should carry the same.
640 BCE: the occupation becomes annexation (next event).

640 BCE: Ashurbanipal takes Susiana (hatched occupation). In 646 'he devastated Susiana with ease, and sacked Susa'; 'Humban-Haltash III was captured in 640 BC, and Ashurbanipal annexed and destroyed the country'. The Humban-Haltash page dates the fall of Susa and his capture to 647, names Madaktu as taken first and quotes 'I devastated the provinces of Elam and on their lands I sowed salt'. 'A weak and fragmented Elamite rule was resurrected soon after with Shuttir-Nakhkhunte' and 'Elamite royalty in the final century preceding the Achaemenids was fragmented among different small kingdoms' (Elam page), so the Assyrian hold is booked as an occupation, not an annexation; Cliopatria draws Elam in Khuzestan until -601 (K16, K17). [fixer me-01: type changed from loss to occupation_start to agree with the keyframes; the page says 'annexed and destroyed', which is the disagreement. neo-assyrian-empire (me-02) should carry the same with roles reversed.]

612 BCE: the Assyrian hold on Susiana ends and Elamite kings return under Median suzerainty. Elam 'was incorporated into the Median Empire (612–546 BC)'; the Assyrian hold ended with Nineveh. The pages name no Elamite king of these years; the median-kingdom dossier (me-05) should carry the vassalage (-612..-550). [fixer me-01: type changed from gain to occupation_end, the pair of the occupation above.]

region.text: Susiana and the Elamite highland: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'

ledger.note: 539 BCE: Elam ends in the Persian empire. Infobox 'Dates: 3200–539 BC', 'Followed by: Achaemenid Empire'; the text gives 540 for Achaemenid rule at Susa. Cliopatria ends the row at -601 (the Median shape begins -615); the new keyframe elam_-600 carries the -615 shape to -540.

wars.name: Early Dynastic wars with Sumer (Enmebaragesi, Eannatum)
wars.outcome: 'The Elamites were said to have been defeated by Enmebaragesi of Kish c. 2750 BC'; 'Eannatum of Lagash defeated them c. 2450 BC' and destroyed Susa; Awan in turn 'defeated the First Dynasty of Ur, probably in the 25th century BC'. Raids and a short occupation, no border.

wars.name: Akkadian campaigns in Elam
wars.outcome: Sargon defeated 'four leaders of Elam, led by the king of Awan' (Luh-ishan, d. c. 2325) and 'the governors, viceroys, and kings of Susa, Waraḫše, and neighboring districts became vassals of Akkad'; Rimush defeated Emahsini; Naram-Sin signed a treaty with Awan's Khita or Helu; Elam 'declared independence' under Kutik-Inshushinak as Akkad weakened.
wars.note: Vassal tint -2290..-2210 in the Akkad dossier; the chronology of Kutik-Inshushinak (c. 2240 or c. 2110) is disputed between the pages.

wars.name: Ur III campaigns against Elam and Anshan
wars.outcome: Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories, then conquered Susa'; Shulgi's year names: 'The governor of Anšan took the king's daughter into marriage' (30), 'Anshan was destroyed' (34), Kimash and Hurti destroyed (45–46); Shu-Sin 'destroyed the land of Zabshali' (his sixth year); Ibbi-Sin's campaigns 'against Anshan, Huhnur, and Susa ceased after his fourteenth year'.

wars.name: Fall of Ur
wars.outcome: Kindattu 'invaded and conquered Ur c. 2004 BC, and captured Ibbi-Sin'; the Elamites 'settled there' until Ishbi-Erra 'ousted the Elamite garrison from Ur' (his 16th year and 'some years later'; the Shimashki page: 21 years).

wars.name: Elamite intervention in Mesopotamia

zones.text: Eshnunna and the Diyala; war with Der

wars.outcome: Siwe-palar-huppak invaded Eshnunna with Babylonian and Mariote help (Zimri-Lim's 10th–11th years), then turned on his allies; 'Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites' (Elam page). Rim-Sin 'had refused to support Hammurabi in his war against Elam'.

wars.name: Kassite–Elamite wars
wars.outcome: Kurigalzu II 'temporarily occupied Elam around 1320 BC'; Kashtiliash IV 'fought Elam unsuccessfully' (c. 1230); Kiddin-Khutran defeated Enlil-nadin-shumi in 1224 and Adad-shuma-iddina c. 1222–1217. Raids; no lasting border change.

wars.name: Shutruk-Nakhunte's conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: 'Shutruk-Nakhunte invaded Kassite Babylonia in the year 1158 BC'; 'Under his command, Elam defeated the Kassites'; Babylonia passed to the Second Dynasty of Isin from c. 1153 (Isin page). The page gives no withdrawal date.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar I's Elamite campaign
wars.outcome: Launched from Dēr in the summer, the Babylonians 'routed the Elamite king Ḫulteludiš-Inšušinak on the banks of the river Ulaya'; 'The campaign destroyed Elam as a power'; no annexation, and 'No contemporary or later source records a sack of Susa' (the Elam page says Susa was sacked). The Shutruk-Nakhunte page dates it 1120, Nebuchadnezzar's own page only within r. c. 1121–1100.

wars.name: Assyrian–Elamite wars
wars.outcome: Sennacherib 'invad[ed] and ravag[ed] Elam' (694), Halule (691); Ashurbanipal: Ulaï (653) and the occupation of Susa, the sack of Susa (646; the Humban-Haltash page: 647, with 'I devastated the provinces of Elam and on their lands I sowed salt'), Humban-Haltash III captured (640) and the country 'annexed and destroyed'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line in three millennia: Susiana's plain edge toward Sumer, the Zagros highland (Awan, Shimashki, Anshan) and the Gulf coast of Fars are all approximate; the only dated lines are Mesopotamian occupations (Ur 2004–1983, Eshnunna 1767–1760, Babylonia 1158–1153) drawn hatched.

sources.title: Elam
sources.note: Infobox 3200–539 BC, no capital, no area; the period chronology; Sargon, Kutik-Inshushinak, 2004, Hammurabi c. 1760, Kassite wars, 1158, the dark age, the Assyrian wars 743–640, Media and 540.

sources.title: Awan dynasty
sources.note: Peli c. 2500, Awan's conjectured location, Enmebaragesi c. 2750, Eannatum c. 2450, Luh-ishan, Naram-Sin's treaty, Kutik-Inshushinak c. 2240, Ur-Nammu's victory.

sources.title: Kutik-Inshushinak
sources.note: Vassal of Akkad since Sargon, independence under Shar-kali-sharri, Eshnunna and Akkad early in Ur-Nammu's reign, Susa overrun by Ur.

sources.title: Shimashki dynasty
sources.note: Dates (three sets), Masjed Soleyman, Kindattu 2004, the 21-year occupation of Ur, Eshnunna marriage.

sources.title: Sukkalmah dynasty
sources.note: Founded c. 1980, seat Susa, Siwe-palar-huppak and Eshnunna, Zimri-Lim's years 10–11, rulers to c. 1450.

sources.title: Shutruk-Nakhunte
sources.note: Reign 1184–1155, the 1158 invasion, Babylon, Sippar, Eshnunna, 'most of Mesopotamia', Nebuchadnezzar I in 1120.

sources.title: Nebuchadnezzar I
sources.note: Reign c. 1121–1100, the Ulaya campaign, no sack of Susa recorded.

sources.title: Humban-Haltash III
sources.note: Humban-Tahrid dynasty c. 830–521, Madaktu, Susa 647, the salt.

sources.title: Kindattu
sources.note: Reign c. 2028–2001, Ur c. 2004, the Elamites settled at Ur, Ishbi-Erra's year 16.

sources.title: Third Dynasty of Ur
sources.note: Ibbi-Sin's campaigns against Susa ceased after year 14; the fall c. 2004; Shu-Sin and Zabshali.

sources.title: Shulgi
sources.note: Anshan year names 30 and 34; Susa held since Puzur-Inshushinak.

sources.title: Lagash
sources.note: Eannatum 'defeated mountainous Elam'; Enannatum I c. 2425.

sources.title: Isin
sources.note: Ishbi-Erra 2018–1985; Isin II c. 1153–1022.

sources.title: Ishbi-Erra
sources.note: Elamite victory in his 16th year, garrison ousted from Ur.

sources.title: Mari, Syria
sources.note: Zimri-Lim's enthronement c. 1776, for the Eshnunna dates.

sources.title: Uruk period
sources.note: Susa II (c. 3700–3100) in the Uruk expansion.

sources.title: Proto-Elamite
sources.note: Would not load: WebFetch returned 641 characters (image captions) twice. The Proto-Elamite dates come from the Elam page instead.

sources.title: Ur-Nammu
sources.note: Reign c. 2112-2094; defeated a coalition of Kutik-Insusinak and cities including Tutub and Eshnunna; an area in the northeast under Elam in the interregnum; conquest of Lagash.

sources.title: Rimush
sources.note: Re-read for the fixer: campaigns against Elam and Marhashi; Elam ruled by Akkadian military governors starting with Eshpum; a seal of a Governor of Elam and vassal of Rimush and Manishtushu; Overlord of Elam c. 2279-2270.

sources.title: Ibbi-Sin
sources.note: Re-read for the fixer: year 14 campaign overwhelming Susa, Adamdun and Awan; Huhnuri and Anshan in year 9; left with only the city of Ur; Shimashki and Elam to dwell in Ur.

notes:
ONE DOSSIER, NOT SPLIT: Cliopatria's 'Elam' row (-3200..-601, 17 shapes) spans Proto-Elamite, Old (Awan, Shimashki, Sukkalmah), Middle (Kidinuid, Igihalkid, Shutrukid) and Neo-Elamite Elam. The Wikipedia article treats these as dynasties of one civilisation seated at Susa and Anshan, so by rule 2 they are rename events (-2500, -2100, -1970, -1500, -1400, -1210, -1100, -830) in one dossier with one colour. The reviewer may prefer a split at the three-century dark age (c. 1100–830): if so, 'Neo-Elamite kingdom' (slug neo-elamite-kingdom, -830..-539) would take the shapes from -900, and this dossier would end -1100 with 'dissolve' to nobody. Not done here.

END YEAR: Cliopatria ends Elam at -601 because its Median shape begins -615; the infobox runs to 539 ('In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'). A new keyframe elam_-600 (-600..-540) extends the last shape, and the dissolve goes to achaemenid-empire. The median-kingdom dossier (me-05) should record Elam as a vassal -612..-550 ('incorporated into the Median Empire (612–546 BC)'); the neo-assyrian-empire dossier (me-02) should record the occupation of Susa (653) and of Susiana (640–612, hatched occupation since the me-01 fix) with roles reversed; babylonia (me-02) the occupation of Elam c. 1320 and the loss of Babylonia 1158–1153.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS CORRECTED: the gap -2700..-2201 filled with a new Awan-period keyframe (Khuzestan + Ilam); the Iraqi arms of the -2000 and -1800 shapes removed (the pages give Ur, Eshnunna and Der as occupations or allies, never Elamite land); the -1150 shape (Babylonia Elamite for fifty years) marked wrong, the conquest kept as a 1158–1153 occupation. The -1100 to -800 shapes are unverified beyond the dynasty dates: the pages are silent on extent in the dark age.

DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES: Kutik-Inshushinak c. 2240–2220 (Elam, Awan pages, long chronology) versus a contemporary of Ur-Nammu 2112–2094 (his own page); Awan founded c. 2400 or c. 2600 or Peli c. 2500; Shimashki c. 2100–1970 (Elam) / c. 2100–1900 / c. 2120–1980 (its page); Sukkalmah c. 1970 (Elam) / c. 1980 (its page) to c. 1770 / 1500 / 1450; the Elamite garrison at Ur ended in Ishbi-Erra's year 16 (c. 2002) or after 21 years (c. 1983); the fall of Susa to Ashurbanipal 646 (Elam) or 647 (Humban-Haltash III); Nebuchadnezzar I sacked Susa (Elam page) or no source records it (his page), and 1120 (Shutruk-Nakhunte page) versus undated.

GAZETTEER: Susa resolves; Anshan (Tall-e Malyan), Madaktu, Hidalu, Chogha Zanbil, Der, Eshnunna do not. Persis is used for Anshan's Fars. Page budget: 9 of 9 opened for Elam (Elam, Awan, Kutik-Inshushinak, Shimashki, Sukkalmah, Shutruk-Nakhunte, Nebuchadnezzar I, Humban-Haltash III, Kindattu) plus the failed Proto-Elamite page; the Igihalkid and Neo-Elamite extents and the Elamite kings of 640–540 remain gaps.

ME-01 FIXES (after the review): (1) /ledger Susa occupation -2450..-2425 now names lagash, not the collective. (2) Akkad's lordship over Susa is booked here too: vassal_start -2290, vassal_end -2210, counterpart akkadian-empire (both years bridged, confidence 1). (3) Persis -2240 is gained from akkadian-empire, not from nobody (Manishtushu 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum', Akkadian Empire page; 'conquered the city of Anshan in Elam', Naram-Sin page); the Awan dynasty page says 'The capital of Anshan ... was never reached by Akkad', so the pages disagree and the reviewer's other option (drop the plateau from akkadian-empire_-2250) was not taken; the region is the Anshan core, not all of Persis. (4) The conquest of Akkad and Eshnunna is re-dated from -2110 to c. -2125 (bridged, confidence 1): the Kutik-Inshushinak page (headed Puzur-Inshushinak) is silent on the year but ties the conquests to the weakening of the Gutians before Utu-hengal's revolt (c. 2119); Akkad is gained from gutian-dynasty (mirror there), the Diyala from nobody; keyframe elam_-2200 now holds -2200..-2126 and elam_-2125 adds Akkad and Diyala to -2101. The page does not mention the Diyala by name (Eshnunna, Tutub and Zimudar are Diyala cities); the dossier keeps the Diyala as the region of those cities. (5) K4 (-2000..-1801) unites the Fars core back (the Cliopatria shape drops Anshan though the Elam page has the Old Elamite state 'centered in Anshan'); the reviewer suggested the region Persis, but that is 620 cells against 105 in every Cliopatria Anshan shape, so the -2100 shape is used. (6) The Assyrian hold of -640..-612 is a hatched occupation, not a loss: I disagree with the Elam page's 'annexed and destroyed' only so far as the same page says 'a weak and fragmented Elamite rule was resurrected soon after'; the shape of -650 is 182/189 cells Khuzestan, so the 'highland remnant' the reviewer suggested would be nothing, and Cliopatria draws no Elam shape for -630..-616, now filled by elam_-630. (7) Capitals: Susa is split around Anshan (-2094..-2016) and the Assyrian years (no seat drawn -640..-613). (8) Predecessor uruk-period and found counterpart added. Not done: the thin items for the dark age -1100..-701 (List of rulers of Elam), Ur-Nammu's reconquest, Ibbi-Sin's Susa, the loss of Babylonia -1153 and Median Susiana -612 were not opened.

AKKAD'S LORDSHIP (me-01 fixer): the vassal pair -2290..-2210 follows the Awan dynasty page ('the low-lying, westerly parts of Elam became a vassal of Akkad, centred at Susa'). The Rimush page, opened for this fix, is stronger: 'Elam would be ruled by Akkadian Military Governors, starting with Eshpum', a seal of 'Governor of Elam and vassal of Rimush and Manishtushu', and the table 'Overlord of Elam c. 2279 – c. 2270 BC'; the Naram-Sin page has 'permanent Akkadian administrative and military settlements' at Susa. Susiana may therefore have been Akkadian provinces rather than a vassal state for part of -2290..-2210; the lighter tint is kept as the reviewer asked. THIN ITEMS: the Ibbi-Sin page (opened) has year 14 'overwhelmed Susa, Adamdun and Awan like a storm' and year 9 an expedition to Huhnuri and Anshan, but no year for Susa passing to the Shimashki, so -2015 stays bridged; the Ur-Nammu and Second Dynasty of Isin pages say nothing on Susa -2094 or the end of the Elamite hold on Babylonia -1153; the dark age -1100..-701, Proto-Elamite, the Medes (-612) and the List of rulers of Elam pages were not opened.
